newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela CANTV global share issue set for mid Nov.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela CANTV global share issue set for mid Nov.

text.p: The forthcoming global issue of 40 percent of government-owned shares in Venezuelan telephone company CANTV will be carried out simultaneously on local and foreign stock markets in mid November, a source close to the issue said Thursday.
"There is a timetable under which supposedly in mid-November the shares are placed both in Venezuela and abroad in one process," the source, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
The price of the shares, part of a 49 percent stake held by the government, would be determined by a book building process in the weeks leading up to the issue, the source added.
Government officials have said between five and 10 percent of CANTV will be offered on local stock markets. Another nine percent has been set aside for workers.
CANTV was partially privatized in 1991 when the VenWorld consortium led by GTE Corp bought a 40 percent stake. Workers bought another 11 percent of the company.
The government has said it plans to offer workers a further nine percent of the company as part of this year's sell-off.

The VenWorld consortium is led by GTE Corp with a 51 percent stake. Local utility Electricidad de Caracas holds 16 percent, Telefonica de Espana 16 percent, local bank Banco Mercantil 12 percent and AT&T five percent.
